records.title: Deliver Agent Property Marketing and Content Publishing
records.body:
Business objective: Agents prepare authorized property content once and manage internal drafts before approved official social publishing becomes available.

Existing behavior: real Agent accounts, profile verification, accepted listing representation, tours and scoped operational workspaces. No Marketing Hub, private marketing library or draft persistence was found after reconciling all repository issues.

Scope: apps/owner-web Agent Portal, apps/api and necessary local migrations. Owner Portal is preserved. Phase 0 governance/architecture and Phase 1 internal navigation, private uploads, authorized property media, persisted drafts and previews are authorized. Phase 2 Meta OAuth/publishing, Phase 3 TikTok/workers/scheduling, Phase 4 optional MCP are not authorized.

Journey: switch explicitly to Agent workspace, open Marketing Hub, choose an authorized property, upload or select media, edit a caption, preview and save a draft. Channels, calendar and performance show accurate unavailable states without fake connected accounts or metrics.

Architecture: Clean and Hexagonal NestJS module with pure domain, granular use cases, repository/storage/processor ports and PostgreSQL/Supabase adapters. Next.js uses existing shell, session store, HttpClient and centralized scoped Zustand state. Client role selection is not authority.

Security: verify live Agent, separate owned media, active accepted property representation and future destination permissions. Private signed media, bounded size/quotas, safe deletion, RLS and revocation checks. No OAuth tokens in client/model. Official provider app reviews, business verification, permissions, secret encryption, consent and callback requirements remain release blockers.

Dependencies: existing #17 coordination, #56/#57/#58 representation, #62/#63/#64 dashboards, #86/#87/#88 Storybook and #103/#107/#112/#113 auth/onboarding. Do not duplicate or close those scopes. No assigned sprint, assignee or invented dates.

Definition of Done: authorized internal CRUD and storage work, cross Agent denials, role navigation isolation, browser/accessibility evidence and required tests reviewed. Full epic is not Done until separately authorized later phases, real provider confirmations and production acceptance. No push/merge/deploy or remote migration in current work.

records.title: Publishing API Feasibility and Architecture
records.body:
Tracking key: MKT-001

## Classification

Parent: WSP.EPIC.AGENT.MARKETING, under platform initiative #12, not Authentication. Type: Story. Domain: Partners. Surface: Owner Web / Backend API. Layer: Cross Stack. Priority: P0. Phase: 0. Status: Ready. Dependencies: repository audit. Sprint and assignee: unassigned.

## User Story

As an authorized Property Agent, I want publishing api feasibility and architecture, so that I can prepare property marketing within my actual permissions and understand the delivery status.

## Existing and Target Behavior

Existing Agent and Owner workspaces and representation rules remain authoritative. Marketing functionality is absent. This story adds only its named capability and reuses existing architecture. Phase 0 is authorized within the internal foundation scope.

## Technical Subtasks

- [ ] Compare official Facebook Page, Instagram professional and TikTok contracts; record app review and token requirements.
- [ ] Separate content lifecycle from per destination publication outcome; document internal ports and release gates.
- [ ] Validate server identity, cross Agent/property scope and negative authorization cases for this capability.
- [ ] Execute meaningful automated checks, document failure recovery and add browser evidence for visible states.
- [ ] Update documentation and acceptance evidence without marking implementation as production acceptance.

## Acceptance Criteria

AC-01: Document official source URLs and the Meta documentation rate limit without claiming verified app permissions.
AC-02: Record TikTok private visibility restriction for unaudited clients and creator consent requirements.
AC-03: No provider request, OAuth credential store or publishing worker is added in Phase 1.

## Walkthrough and Verification

Open the Agent workspace and follow the relevant publishing api feasibility and architecture action. Exercise valid input and permitted scope, then invalid input, unavailable service and another Agent/property identifier. Verify the stored result or an explicit safe refusal. Visible views must have loading, empty and error/retry states, labeled controls, focus visibility and responsive checks at 375x812, 834x1112, 1440x900 and 1920x1080. Non UI stories verify API/SQL contracts and do not fabricate screenshots.

Positive tests demonstrate the accepted result. Negative tests demonstrate invalid data, revoked authorization and cross scope denial. Backend changes require isolated PostgreSQL/RLS tests, storage changes require failed transfer and credential handling checks. Future provider work requires provider sandbox evidence after approval, never browser automation or credential scraping.

## Definition of Done and Boundaries

Every AC has source/test/review evidence; known limitations are explicit and linked prerequisites are resolved. A local implementation is In Review, not Done. Future phases, remote migrations, provider app changes, publishing, workers, paid dependencies, push and deployment are excluded from current authorization.

Documentation: docs/agile/marketing/specification.md and docs/agile/marketing/feasibility.md (local, not yet committed). Linked child task implements the concrete architectural subtasks above; no duplicate Agent account or dashboard is created.
